rule: Every backend audit storage plan must include a write fixture with payload, validation, expected result, rollback fixture, and blocked payment-route test before implementation begins.
phase_one_guardrail: No rental payment, deposit, escrow, payout, booking commission, payment-custody signal, tenant-private memory, or unvalidated storage fixture can reach backend implementation in phase one.
fixture_principles: Turn each backend audit storage plan into a copy-ready write fixture.
Keep payload name, tenant id, record id, write route, expected result, validation state, rollback fixture, and blocked route together.
Separate fixture metadata from tenant-private proof payloads.
Require a blocked payment-route test beside every allowed write fixture.
Make validation and rollback expectations visible before backend code is written.
Keep fixtures role-aware for buyer, supplier, and founder storage paths.
Use static fixtures until real auth, database, and API tests exist.

role_write_fixtures.validation_state: supplier tenant and success role required
founder workspace and admin review required

acceptance: Marketplace shows Storage Write Fixture Pack after Backend Audit Storage.
Buyer, supplier, and founder views each show payload name, tenant id, record id, write route, expected result, validation state, rollback fixture, and blocked route.
Copy output explains fixture event, source storage, payload name, tenant id, record id, expected result, validation state, rollback fixture, and blocked payment route.
Build Phase shows the v178 Storage Write Fixture Pack contract after the Backend Audit Storage Plan contract.
Docs include fixture states, fixture routes, blocked payment routes, and required fixture fields.
Static check fails if the fixture UI, contract, JSON model, cache-bust token, or render functions are missing.
No backend implementation starts without a write fixture or explicit hold.
